Cross-Validate a Model on a Dataset

Source: R/resolve.R
resolve.cross_validate.Rd

Train and score the same model recipe on k folds of a dataset's plots: each fold is held out once while the model, restarted from the same initial weights, trains on the others. Folds are drawn at random with seed, or, with spatial, as blocks of a latitude / longitude grid, so a held-out fold is a region the model never saw.

Usage

resolve.cross_validate(dataset, nFolds = 5L, seed = 42L, spatial = NULL, ...)

Arguments

dataset

A ResolveDataset object from resolve.dataset.csv().

nFolds

Number of folds (default 5).

seed

Random seed of the folds (default 42).

spatial

NULL (default) for random folds, or a named list of the spatial block settings: lat_size and lon_size (block size in degrees) and balance (TRUE assigns blocks to folds by greedy bin-packing for folds of similar size, FALSE round-robin); a field left out takes the RESOLVE engine's default (resolve.default_config() "spatial_block"). Needs coordinates.

...

The model and training arguments of resolve.train.dataset() (hiddenDims, maxEpochs, lr, modelConfig, trainConfig, pretrain, ...).

Value

A list with n_folds, mean_metrics and std_metrics (per target and metric, over the folds), fold_results (each fold's training result, as result of resolve.train.dataset()) and total_time_seconds.

Examples

plots <- system.file("extdata", "plots.csv", package = "resolveR")
species <- system.file("extdata", "species.csv", package = "resolveR")
roles <- list(plot_id = "plot_id", species_id = "species", abundance = "cover",
              genus = "genus", family = "family", latitude = "lat", longitude = "lon")
targets <- list(elevation = list(column = "elevation", task = "regression"),
                habitat = list(column = "habitat", task = "classification"))
dataset <- resolve.dataset.csv(plots, species, roles = roles, targets = targets)
cv <- resolve.cross_validate(dataset, nFolds = 3L, maxEpochs = 10L)
cv$mean_metrics$elevation$r2

blocks <- resolve.cross_validate(dataset, nFolds = 3L, maxEpochs = 10L,
                                 spatial = list(lat_size = 0.2, lon_size = 0.3))
